units.text: INT. MUSEUM VENTILATION DUCT - NIGHT
A square steel tunnel, barely wider than shoulders.
A penlight clenched in teeth throws a thin beam ahead.
NELL PARISH, 30s, black bodysuit, crawls on her elbows toward a grate.
She stops.
Listens.
Under her, far below, a floor polisher whines and fades.
She starts again, slower, dragging a duffel behind her by a strap.
A tiny recorder clipped to her collar clicks and plays her own voice, recorded days ago, flat and rehearsed.
Guard's on the east wing at the top of the hour. Four minutes, no more.
units.name: NELL

units.text: She does not react.
She reaches the grate and peers through.
Below is a gallery, pale, a single painting lit on the far wall.
She takes the penlight out of her mouth and clicks it off.
She works a screwdriver into the first bolt.
It turns.
The second.
The third sticks.
She breathes out, wipes her palm on her thigh, tries again, and it gives with a squeal that echoes along the duct.
She freezes.
Below, the polisher stops.
Footsteps, slow, heavy, approaching.
A flashlight beam crosses the gallery floor and slides up the wall.
It passes the grate.
It passes again.
She holds her breath until the beam moves on.
Three minutes. Do not rush the rope.
units.name: NELL

units.text: She lifts the grate out, lays it in the duct, and rolls onto her back.
She unclips a coil of rope from her belt, ties it to a bracket, tests the knot with her full weight.
Then she feeds the rope through the opening, lowers herself over the edge, and hangs there, boots swinging three meters above the parquet.
She drops the last meter.
Lands in a crouch.
Silent.
She crosses to the painting, a small landscape in a heavy frame.
She runs two fingers around the wire.
Pulls a thin cutter.
Snips.
The frame sags.
Behind her, a door handle turns.
If you hear the handle, you're already late.
units.name: NELL

units.text: She doesn't stop.
She slips the canvas free of the frame, rolls it into a tube, shoves it into her duffel, and runs.
The door opens as she reaches the rope.
She climbs, hand over hand, as a flashlight beam swings up through the gap.
She makes the grate.
Pulls the rope up after her.
Drags the grate back across the opening, and lies flat in the dark, her heart loud in her ears.
Below, the guard's boots stop under the vent.
A long moment.
Then they turn and walk away.
She reaches up and switches off the recorder.
She smiles in the dark.
